Young Heroes

By: Mart-Marie Faure | Production

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Two twelve year old boys risked their own lives to help survivors of the Kroonstad train crash.

Unique Selling Point:
On the 4th of January two twelve year old boys, Evert du Preez and Mokoni Chaka witnessed the fatal passanger train crash between Henneman and Kroonstad. Fearlessly the two boys rushed to the scene of the accident and bravely assisted the injured.

Summary:
On the fourth of January the Shosholoza Meyl passenger train on its way from Port Elizabeth to Johannesburg, collided with a truck at a level crossing at the Geneva station between Henneman and Kroonstad. A Klerksdorp truck driver had driven his vehicle onto the railway crossing. The passenger train ploughed into it. The du Preez farmhouse is about a 100 metres away from the railway line and the scene of the accident. the du Preez family, including their 12 year old son Evert and his friend Mokoni, with some of the farmworkers rushed to the scene of the accident. The locomotive and front carriages had derailed and a thick cloud of dust was hanging over the scene. About 10 minutes later a fire broke out. Screams echoed from the front carriages as the flames engulfed the mangled wreck. the two twelve year old boys fearlessly helped to pull babies children and the elderly from the train.

Press Release:


Young Heroes
At just 12 years old, their selfless efforts to assist victims of the Kroonstad train crash have earned them the admiration of the entire nation. After witnessing the incident, the two boys fearlessly rushed to the scene to help the injured, pulling babies and the elderly from the train. Carte Blanche meets young South African heroes Evert du Preez and Mokoni Chaka.


Script:


Young Heroes

MacFarlane on Camera It was this at this level crossing more than 3 weeks ago on the 4th of January where a horrific train crash left 21 people dead and many others injured.

V/O

Four hundred and twenty nine passengers were on the Shosoloza Meyl when it collided with a truck between Hennenman and Kroonstad. Just two hundred metres away on the du Preez farm twelve year old Evert du Preez and best friend Mokoni Chaka witnessed the crash.

Evert/ Mokoni I saw a lorry coming from loading grain and then the driver didn't see the train. Then it collided with the train. I came from the horses to the house and I saw smoke, we ran to it, me and my friend.

V/O Dumisane Hopa, his wife and daughter were passengers on the train

Dumisani Hopa It was a safe journey all the way from Port Elizabeth, it was safe. Nobody could tell that there is something disastrous waiting for us in front.

V/O They had just finished their breakfast when the accident occurred.

Dumisani Hopa We had some coffee, they put some coffee and as the waiter was leaving that is the time the first knock happened. And then the second knock happened just seconds after. And then the dishes in the kitchen, we could tell there is something now terribly wrong. And then the 3rd knock mow of which even the water from the kitchen, the hot water from the urns just came

falling down.

Evert

When this accident happened where were your parents? They were up there. They were working. When we ran there my father came with a tractor.

UPSOUND Evert & Mokone Maar het julle nie geskrik nie? Was julle nie bang nie? Ons was. Was julle 'n bietjie bang? Ja. Hoeveel mense was daar? Daar was baie. Daar was baie mense. Party van hulle is vasgekeer, ander besig om te brand.

Dumisani Hopa That is when I started noticing these two boys. They were carrying things, bringing some people, helping, you see.

V/o Flames engulfed some of the carriages and people trapped inside were pleading for help. Bravely young Mokone climbed into one of the carriages to try and save those trapped inside.

Mokone We took them out through the window. My friend was standing outside. I gave him the baby through the window.

Evert I was next to the train. I climbed up the wreckage next to the window. As I was calling him Mokone was helping the people in the train.

V/o Eventually the situation in and around the train became desperate.

Dumisane As the ambulances started coming they were just looking for anybody

they can help. Anybody, because some people were lying on the streets, some people were crying looking for their people, so there was all that going up and down of the people.

V/o For safety reasons people were kept away from the carriages.

Dumisane The people were screaming from inside the train, inside the train asking for help. And as the fire was now starting to become more and more those screams because of also the smoke, people are inhaling the smoke – now the voices were actually coming down coming down coming down...

UPSOUND Evert & Mokone Aren't you scared when you think about it? Yes. Is it still haunting you? Yes. Do you sleep at night? Yes. 'n Person cannot sleep because it is very sad to hear those people cry and dying in there.

Mokone When you are at home and sleeping, don't you see those people in your sleep? I hear them crying in my sleep but when I am awake I hear nothing. What are your parents saying when you're telling them this? They say I mustn't be scared I must just sleep.

David Sometimes he calls me in the middle of the night. Then I ask him what it is. I think it must be this incident that's accident that is affecting him.

LINK The heroic feat of these two young boys has not gone unnoticed. They have now been nominated for the Order of Mendi for Bravery.

V/O After reading about their story in the newspaper Renier Schoeman felt so inspired that he decided to put Evert and Mokoni’s names forward for this prestigious honour.

Renier I served in President Mandela's cabinet for 2 years – the first cabinet after the new dispensation – and I just know how committed he was first of all to children but also to the whole concept of reconciliation in this country and a colour-blind South Africa. And as the Freedom Charter says South Africa is a country that belongs to all who live in it, black and white and that was his vision and that vision should be manifested and I think in this case it was.

Evert Ek voel baie trots op myself en ek is bly ek het dit gedoen want ek het 'n voorbeeld gestel vir die mense in Suid-Afrika om nie net aan hulle self te dink nie en ander mense wat langs hulle ook is.

Mokone It makes me feel good.

V/o Evert's mother, Julie was on the scene and witnessed the boys bravery.

Julie Hulle het nie gedink aan enige gevaar of wat met hulle kon gebeur het nie, so ek is baie trots op hulle ja.

V/O

These two remarkable boys have shared a special friendship from a very young age.

Julie Hulle is van kleins af vriende en hulle is amper onafskeidbaar.Hulle is baie erg oor mekaar.

Renier I think for a young white boy and a young black boy spontaneously in the

given situation such as this, of great pressure to just instinctively do the right thing and take care to help people who are in dire danger and in need, and that's what these two youngsters did. Nobody told them to do it. They could've walked away and said ooh look at this how bad. But they didn't. They put their heads down and they did it. It's that sort of can-do but also a positive attitude to life that that gives us reason to be optimistic what can happen in this country on the road ahead.

V/o During the course of the day Evert and Mokone rescued several passengers who were trapped in the carriages, and later when it became too dangerous, they supplied the traumatised and injured with water from the farm.

Dumisane There was a - I don't know if it's Mama Du Preez's mother who was on the other side of the fence giving them water. And there the fence is so much and there's a dip. And they said no gooi. Gooi and then they catch. And then rush to give the people the water. Whatever those boys did was so so... I don't want to say it was out of this world and other people wouldn't have done it. But really it was out of this world.
